instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Six years on from QPR, two of them outside the top flight; a durable, limited left-back who was a slightly better player at 31 than at 25.
Back in England at 33 after three seasons at Helsingborg; the reading and the technique survived, the pace did not.
Excellent alongside Stam in the treble season; a genuinely good centre-half whose career was cut short by injury rather than a limit of ability.
Eleven starts; the knee trouble that eventually forced him out of Manchester United had begun to cost him whole months.
A season at Barcelona in between; back in England at 30 as a good, aggressive holding midfielder rather than the passer who had won a Double and a World Cup.
Twenty-one years old, captain of a side that reached an FA Cup final, and five goals from central midfield.
Technically the best player in a mid-table Sunderland side at 19; later an Olympic gold medallist with Argentina. Rated on ability, not on Sunderland’s league position.
Technically the best midfielder in a Forest side that finished third; a genuine goal threat from deep.
Sixteen league goals from the wing; genuinely one of the most dangerous wide players in Europe that season.
Sharp fall in output and influence before the Fiorentina move; the level dropped with it.

Four years, Fiorentina and Rangers on from Everton, and on loan at a relegated Manchester City at 31; seven starts, no goals, and none of the directness that made him an 86. The eight-point fall is spread across four seasons away.
The reigning Champions League winner, and when fit the best defender in the record-breaking Chelsea back line — quick, aggressive in the tackle and a superb reader of a through ball.
The best defender in a back four that conceded 24; reading and recovery a clear level above the partner who got the headlines.
Thirty-five starts in a Liverpool side that finished second conceding thirty; shot-stopping and reflexes of a clearly elite standard in his first English season.
The season of the Old Trafford errors and the confidence that went with them; the raw ability was unchanged, the reliability that is part of a goalkeeper’s ability was not.
Five starts, the place gone to Reina, and thirty-two years old; competent when called on and no longer a first choice anywhere.
Twenty-one league goals, but eleven of them penalties, for a side that went down. Genuinely explosive pace and a sharp finisher; limited in the air and in link play, so good rather than elite.
Seven starts across an injury-wrecked season; the pace that was the whole of his game had started to go with the knee.
Age 37, seven starts for a relegated Wednesday; a long way past his level.
Regular left-back in the Ipswich side that finished fifth; his best season.
Ever-present in the side that finished second with 86 points; twelve goals from wide right and the hardest running in the league.
Converted back to a forward after joining Ipswich.
A difficult first English season, played wide before the move into central midfield settled him.
Thirty-four and displaced by Cudicini; six starts in his last Chelsea season.
Capped by England in 1991; this was his comeback season after a cruciate injury.
Thirty-one, four starts, and three seasons after his last regular top-flight football; the pace that made the crossing dangerous had gone.
A genuine late developer — a fringe player at 24, a first-choice Premier League midfielder at 30.
Captain of a Southampton side that reached the FA Cup final; a genuinely useful left-sided midfielder at 33, and no more than that.
Nine starts after a January arrival, still adjusting to the speed of the league; the defender he became arrives the following August, and the jump to 88 is a real change rather than drift.
Half of the best defence in Europe, in a side that conceded 22 and won the European Cup.
PFA Player of the Year and fourteen consecutive clean sheets; the best season by a centre-half in the league since Ferdinand the year before.
Still the best left foot in the squad, but the application and the end product both dropped.
Three seasons at Celtic in between; back in England at 30 with the vision intact and the sharpness reduced - eight assists in a mid-table City side.
Four goals in 24 starts for a Bradford side relegated with 26 points; the least effective season of a modest top-flight career.
Six years and a spell at Marseille apart; the 20-year-old at Oldham and the established Sunderland right-back are not the same footballer.
Three starts; lost the shirt amid the match-fixing trial.
Cruciate injury in November ended his season and effectively his Chelsea career.
